curation.lead:
Peter Andreas Thiel (born October 11, 1967, Frankfurt am Main) is a German-American billionaire technology investor, co-founder of PayPal and Palantir Technologies, and founding partner of Founders Fund. With an estimated net worth of $27.5 billion and triple citizenship in the United States, Germany, and New Zealand, Thiel occupies a singular position at the intersection of Silicon Valley capital, government surveillance infrastructure, and Republican political power. He co-founded PayPal in 1998 (sold to eBay for $1.5 billion in 2002), made the first outside investment in Facebook ($500,000 for 10.2% in 2004), and co-founded Palantir Technologies in 2003 with CIA seed funding via In-Q-Tel. His venture firm Founders Fund now manages approximately $17 billion in assets, and its portfolio includes significant stakes in SpaceX, Anduril Industries, and Stripe. Palantir, where Thiel serves as chairman, earned $970.5 million in government contracts in 2025, providing data analytics to the CIA, NSA, FBI, U.S. Army, ICE, and the Israeli Defense Ministry.

DOJ and House Oversight documents reveal that Thiel maintained a sustained social relationship with Jeffrey Epstein from September 2012 through at least November 2018, seven months before Epstein's arrest. The introduction was brokered by Ian Osborne, a UK-based fixer in Epstein's network (EFTA02724710). Over the following six years, at least twenty direct emails were exchanged between Thiel (peter@thielcapital.com) and Epstein (jeevacation@gmail.com), and at least seven in-person meetings are documented at Epstein's residence at 9 East 71st Street and at Thiel Capital's San Francisco office. Epstein's assistant Lesley Groff classified Thiel as a "VIP" in scheduling correspondence (EFTA02327970). A March 2012 seminar invite list placed Thiel alongside Marc Andreessen, Jeff Bezos, Bill Gates, and Eric Schmidt on Epstein's "MONEY" list (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028784), and a June 2016 custom sweatshirt gift list named Thiel alongside Chomsky, Joi Ito, Reid Hoffman, and Kathryn Ruemmler as Epstein's closest social contacts (EFTA02301988).

A critical finding distinguishes Thiel from figures like Leon Black or Les Wexner: there are zero Deutsche Bank transactions, zero USVI entities, zero UCC filings, and zero shared corporate structures between Thiel and Epstein. The relationship was social and informational, not financial. Epstein's value proposition to Thiel was access: a single day's schedule in October 2014 placed Thiel alongside William Burns (then Deputy Secretary of State and future CIA Director), Kathryn Ruemmler (former White House Counsel), Leon Black (Apollo Global Management), Jabor Al Thani (Qatar royal family), and Terje Roed-Larsen (United Nations) (EFTA02377982). Thiel reciprocated with investment guidance, including direct advice on Palantir secondary share pricing when Epstein was offered a block at $5.50 per share in October 2016 (EFTA02447787, EFTA02447940).

sections.title: The Epstein Relationship: Access, Not Money
sections.content:
The documented relationship between Peter Thiel and Jeffrey Epstein spans from September 2012, when Ian Osborne brokered the introduction (EFTA02724710: "Peter not around on Sunday/Monday. I can give him dates for NY"), through at least November 2018, when Epstein wrote to Thiel asking "Are you enjoying LA?" and Thiel replied "Can't complain thus far" (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_032827). This six-year arc is documented across more than 976 items in the DOJ corpus, making Thiel one of the most extensively documented Silicon Valley contacts in Epstein's records.

The relationship's contours are clear from the email record. Epstein repeatedly invited Thiel to his private island in the U.S. Virgin Islands, to Zorro Ranch in New Mexico, and to his Caribbean properties. Thiel politely declined most of these invitations. In August 2015, Epstein pitched the ranch by describing "quantum computing people" and "some presidents" who would be present, then told Thiel to "invite zuck and wife" because there were "no people for miles and miles no eyes just peace and quiet" (EFTA02491408). Thiel's response referenced an awkward dinner guest: "Will hold off on her... talk soon!" In June 2017, Epstein pushed for a Caribbean visit: "great, or come to caribbean, wayyy overdue." Thiel deflected: "Don't like mosquitoes -- and always hard to get there... will let you know when back in NYC" (EFTA02347109).

Where Thiel did engage consistently was in New York. Multiple confirmed meetings took place at 9 East 71st Street, documented through Groff's scheduling emails. An August 2017 lunch was marked as VIP (EFTA02327970). A November 2017 exchange confirmed a noon lunch: Thiel wrote "Maybe lunch around noon?" and Epstein replied "look forward to it. see you then" (EFTA02229905). The April 2016 meeting was notable for occurring at Thiel Capital's office in San Francisco, with Groff sending detailed parking and dietary instructions (EFTA02466603). Thiel's executive assistants -- Talia in 2014 and Elly Untermeyer in 2017 -- coordinated logistics directly with Epstein's staff.

The investigative significance of negative findings cannot be overstated. Searches of Deutsche Bank transaction records, USVI corporate registries, UCC filings, FAA aircraft registrations, and FARA foreign agent registrations all returned zero results for Thiel or any Thiel entity. Unlike Leon Black, who paid Epstein $158 million through consulting agreements, or Les Wexner, who granted Epstein extraordinary trust architecture, Thiel had no documented financial entanglement with Epstein. The relationship operated on a currency of access and information.

sections.title: Epstein as Network Broker
sections.content:
Epstein's primary function in the Thiel relationship was as a broker of introductions to figures outside Thiel's existing networks -- particularly in diplomacy, intelligence, and Middle Eastern royalty. The most significant documented instance occurred in September 2014, when Epstein arranged for Thiel to meet William "Bill" Burns, then Deputy Secretary of State. Epstein described Burns as "the diplomats diplomat" who had "conducted the secret iran negotiations kept them secret for a year" (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_030215). The same week's schedule (EFTA02377982) placed Thiel at 12pm alongside Burns, Boris Nikolic at 2pm, Jabor Al Thani at 3pm, and Terje Roed-Larsen at 8pm, with Leon Black and Kathryn Ruemmler also listed.

Epstein also brokered a meeting between Thiel and Noam Chomsky in October 2015, writing that he had "spoke to chomsky and told him about you if monday afternoon works it would be just the three of us" (EFTA02484898). In June 2015, Epstein introduced Thiel to Sergey Belyakov, described as "my very good friend that's organizing innovation conference in Moscow" (EFTA02345029). Thiel asked for more context and later mentioned that "they wanted me to come to Moscow not sure if I can do that" (EFTA02494602). During the July 2016 Republican National Convention, Epstein connected Thiel with Tom Barrack, Colony Capital CEO and Trump fundraiser, writing: "He will be a speaker at the convention. He runs Colony Capital. Solid great real estate judgement. Donalds fund raiser" (EFTA02456884).

The brokerage ran in both directions. Epstein leveraged Thiel's name to attract others. In October 2016, Epstein told Jabor Al Thani's nephew: "Peter thiel is with me on fri founder of facebook paypal and palentir" (EFTA02448800), using Thiel's presence as a draw for Gulf royalty. The same month, Thiel and Russian UN Ambassador Vitaly Churkin jointly lunched at 9 East 71st Street, organized by Karyna Shuliak. In September 2016, Epstein had written to Thiel: "sorry you are not here, vitally churkin debriefing on syria, wild." In January 2017, Epstein proposed "geopolitics on the 10th new york. ehud churkin lunch?" -- pairing Thiel with both the Russian UN Ambassador and Ehud Barak, the former Israeli Prime Minister, weeks before Churkin's death in February 2017.

sections.title: The Silicon Valley Dinner Circuit
sections.content:
Thiel was not merely an individual contact but a node in Epstein's systematic cultivation of Silicon Valley's most powerful figures. The most significant documented gathering occurred on August 2, 2015, at Baume Restaurant in Palo Alto, where Epstein hosted a dinner attended by Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan, Peter Thiel, Reid Hoffman, Joi Ito, and MIT neuroscientist Ed Boyden (EFTA02718470). Two days later, Epstein invited Thiel to bring "zuck and wife" to Zorro Ranch. This dinner occurred during the peak of Epstein's Silicon Valley cultivation period (2014-2016) and demonstrates that Epstein was not merely collecting names but orchestrating in-person gatherings of the technology industry's most powerful decision-makers.

Epstein treated Thiel and Reid Hoffman as a linked pair, scheduling them together and monitoring both. In April 2016, Epstein emailed Hoffman: "im waiting on thiel re lunch schedule" (EFTA02465970). Hoffman mentioned a "potus" conversation on a separate thread. A March 2012 seminar planning document (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_028784) placed Thiel on the "MONEY" invite list alongside Andreessen, Bezos, Brin, Gates, Schmidt, Milken, and Simons -- predating the Osborne-mediated introduction by six months and suggesting Thiel was already on Epstein's target list. The June 2016 custom sweatshirt gift list (EFTA02301988) -- naming "valeria chomsky joi martin reid thiel ruemmler and rothschild" -- provides a snapshot of Epstein's closest social circle at the peak of the relationship.

Epstein's inner circle tracked Thiel closely. Richard Kahn forwarded at least six Thiel-related news articles to Epstein between 2017 and 2018, from the New York Times, BuzzFeed, CNBC, and the Wall Street Journal (EFTA02365477, EFTA02539899). Joi Ito forwarded a Thiel/Trump article in May 2016 (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_029500). Epstein himself commented on Thiel's political activities in real time, writing "trump delegate fun" in May 2016 (EFTA02465005) and sharing the Michael Wolff Fire and Fury article in January 2018 (EFTA02543999). The monitoring was mutual in a limited sense: Thiel and Epstein exchanged macro investment views, with Epstein reporting in August 2014 that he had "met with Treasury on Bitcoin lots to talk about interesting tax ramifications" (EFTA02587270) and Thiel sharing a Gompertz Curve mortality paper in June 2015 (EFTA02497395).

sections.title: The Gawker Convergence
sections.content:
A striking temporal overlap connects Thiel's secret litigation campaign against Gawker Media and Epstein's own interest in the outlet's destruction. In January 2015, Gawker reporter John Cook contacted Epstein's associates seeking comment on flight logs he planned to publish (EFTA02513992: "Just got a voicemail from John Cook from Gawker wanting to ask me questions. Said he is going to publish some of your flight logs"). Days later, Epstein emailed Ghislaine Maxwell about Gawker printing "the entire address book, albeit redacted." Maxwell replied that friends were "apoplectic" (EFTA02512162).

This was occurring during the period when Thiel, through intermediary Aron D'Souza, was secretly funding multiple lawsuits against Gawker. Thiel spent over $10 million financing at least four suits, most prominently the Hulk Hogan sex tape case that produced a $140 million jury verdict in March 2016. When that verdict was announced, Kathryn Ruemmler -- Epstein's own attorney and former Obama White House Counsel -- emailed Epstein: "This is amazing and kind of awesome" (EFTA02471435). Epstein's inner circle was celebrating the destruction of the outlet that had been investigating Epstein's flight logs and address book.

There is no direct evidence that Epstein funded or directed the Gawker litigation. However, both Thiel and Epstein had independent reasons to want Gawker destroyed: Thiel over the 2007 outing of his sexuality, and Epstein over the outlet's publication of his address book and flight log investigations. Richard Kahn later forwarded articles about Thiel's bid to purchase Gawker's assets in bankruptcy to Epstein (EFTA02539899), confirming the inner circle's continued interest in the saga's resolution. The convergence of motives, combined with the documented social relationship, remains an area warranting further investigation.

sections.title: The Defense-Intelligence Empire
sections.content:
Palantir Technologies, co-founded by Thiel in 2003 with an initial $2 million CIA seed investment via In-Q-Tel, has grown into one of the most consequential intelligence contractors in American history. Federal contracts grew from $4.4 million in 2009 to $970.5 million in 2025. The company's Gotham platform is used by the CIA, NSA, FBI, and multiple allied intelligence services. Its $10 billion Army TITAN contract, consolidated from 75 separate agreements, and its $480 million Maven contract (expanded by $795 million in 2025) position Palantir as the primary commercial provider of AI-enabled intelligence analytics to the U.S. military. A $30 million ICE "ImmigrationOS" contract (April 2025) tracks deportation operations.

Palantir's relationship with Israeli defense and intelligence deserves particular scrutiny given the broader Epstein network's Israeli intelligence connections. Thiel and CEO Alex Karp met IDF leaders in Tel Aviv. Palantir maintains an office there since 2015. Reporting indicates that Palantir Gotham technology powers IDF targeting systems including those developed by Unit 8200, Israel's signals intelligence directorate. The Carbyne connection provides another link: in May 2018, intermediaries sought to connect Ehud Barak's Carbyne (an Israeli 911-technology startup with intelligence community ties) to Thiel's Founders Fund via Trae Stephens, an ex-Palantir employee. The email chain (EFTA02656963) noted the Palantir background as rationale for the fit.

Founders Fund has extended the defense-technology thesis further through its $2.5 billion investment round in Anduril Industries (June 2025, $1 billion from Founders Fund alone), valuing the autonomous weapons manufacturer at $30.5 billion. Anduril was co-founded by Palmer Luckey and Trae Stephens, who met at a Founders Fund retreat in 2014. The company won a $9 billion autonomous aircraft contract with General Atomics. Palantir's landmark bid protest against the U.S. Army (Palantir USG Inc. v. United States, 1:16-cv-00784, Court of Federal Claims, 2016) established the legal precedent that the Pentagon must consider commercial off-the-shelf software in procurement -- a ruling that opened the floodgates for Thiel-affiliated defense technology companies.

The lobbying infrastructure supporting these contracts began in September 2006, when Palantir first registered lobbyists through Morgan and Cunningham LLC, focused on defense and homeland security. By 2025, Palantir retained at least three simultaneous lobbying firms covering defense, intelligence, law enforcement, and financial institution policy.

sections.title: Political Network and the PayPal Mafia
sections.content:
Thiel's political influence operates through a tightly interlocked network of proteges and co-investors rooted in two institutions: the Stanford Review, which he founded in 1987 as a conservative student newspaper, and PayPal, which he co-founded in 1998. The so-called PayPal Mafia now occupies three of the most powerful positions in the Trump administration: JD Vance as Vice President, Elon Musk running DOGE, and David Sacks as AI and Cryptocurrency advisor. Ken Howery, Thiel's Founders Fund co-founder, served as U.S. Ambassador to Sweden under Trump's first term.

Thiel's mentor-protege relationships are the mechanism of political deployment. He met JD Vance at a Yale Law School speech in 2011, hired him at Mithril Capital, backed his firm Narya Capital, donated $15 million to his 2022 Senate campaign (the largest single-candidate contribution on record at the time), and brought Vance to his first meeting with Trump at Mar-a-Lago in February 2021. He co-wrote Zero to One with Blake Masters, then funded Masters' Arizona Senate campaign with $1.5 million via FEC. Multiple Thiel Capital employees donated to Masters' campaign in a pattern suggesting coordinated support. David Sacks co-authored The Diversity Myth with Thiel at Stanford, served as PayPal COO, and cross-invested through Craft Ventures in Palantir while Founders Fund invested in Yammer.

FEC records confirm Thiel as a major Republican donor: $15 million to Vance, $250,000 to Eric Schmitt (Missouri), $852,000 through Mike Johnson's Grow the Majority committee, and $10,000 contributions to fifteen or more state Republican parties. He is a member of the Federalist Society and has been a Bilderberg Steering Committee member since 2021, having attended meetings from 2007 through 2024. He co-founded Dialog, an invitation-only forum described as a "tech-era Bilderberg" for CEOs, elected officials, and intellectuals. His philanthropic network -- including the Thiel Fellowship (paying students to drop out of college), the Seasteading Institute (floating autonomous cities), and investments in life extension (SENS Research Foundation) and psychedelics (Atai Life Sciences, Compass Pathways with German financier Christian Angermayer) -- reflects a libertarian ideology that treats existing institutions as obstacles to be circumvented rather than reformed.

sections.title: Financial Architecture and Tax Strategy
sections.content:
Thiel's financial structure is notable for its tax optimization and jurisdictional diversification. The most consequential documented strategy is his Roth IRA, which grew from less than $2,000 in 1999 (when he placed pre-IPO PayPal shares into it) to approximately $5 billion by 2021, all tax-free under Roth IRA rules. ProPublica's investigation of this structure revealed that Thiel exploited a vehicle designed for middle-class retirement savings to shelter billions in capital gains from taxation -- an approach that, while apparently legal, prompted congressional scrutiny of Roth IRA contribution rules.

SEC filings under CIK 1211060 (THIEL PETER) show 72 or more filings as insider or owner across Palantir, Meta/Facebook, PayPal, Oscar Health, BlackSky Technology, and at least ten other companies. His business address is listed as 2121 Avenue of the Stars, Suite 3300, Los Angeles. Thiel and his entities are party to or named in more than 30 federal cases across multiple categories. The most consequential securities litigation arose from Facebook's May 2012 IPO, in which Thiel was named as an individual defendant in at least six class action suits (including Lazar v. Facebook, 3:12-cv-03199; Spatz v. Facebook, 3:12-cv-02662; and Alexander v. Facebook, 1:12-cv-04157) alongside Zuckerberg, Andreessen, and other directors. Thiel had sold 16.8 million shares at $38 each for $638 million in the IPO. All cases were consolidated in SDNY MDL 2389. More recently, Cupat v. Palantir Technologies (1:22-cv-02384, D. Colorado) alleged securities fraud by Palantir's board including Thiel, but final judgment was entered in favor of all defendants in April 2025.

Palantir's intellectual property litigation includes the i2 Inc. v. Palantir trade secret case (1:10-cv-00842, EDVA), which alleged theft of proprietary software code and settled within six months. The Palantir v. Abramowitz RICO case (5:19-cv-06879, NDCA) involved allegations against a former engineer and went to jury trial in late 2022. The KT4 Partners shareholder inspection case reached the Delaware Supreme Court (203 A.3d 738, January 2019), establishing precedent for shareholder rights in pre-IPO companies. The DOJ civil forfeiture action against Palantir Series D preferred stock (purchased with stolen 1MDB funds) represents a distinct category of legal exposure where the company's shares were instrumentalized in a foreign corruption scheme without the company's participation.

Palantir's employment discrimination history includes a 2017 DOL/OFCCP settlement of $1.7 million for systematic discrimination against Asian job applicants, followed by individual civil rights suits (Lynch v. Palantir, 3:24-cv-01429, NDCA; Davidson v. Palantir, 3:24-cv-01357, SDCA). The Mithril Capital litigation (McKellar v. Mithril, 1:19-cv-01086, WDTX) -- in which a former employee alleged sexual harassment by co-founder Ajay Royan -- led to Royan's departure from the firm Thiel had co-founded. Thiel was not directly named but was chairman of Mithril's board.
